summary.name: HTTP Toolkit
summary.one_liner: HTTP Toolkit is an open-source tool for intercepting, inspecting, editing, and sending HTTP(S) traffic on Windows, Linux, and Mac.
use_cases: debug HTTP and HTTPS traffic from apps or browsers
intercept Android or iOS app network requests
mock or stub API responses for testing
pause and edit live requests with breakpoints
send custom HTTP requests to explore APIs
fix CORS errors by injecting headers
summary.what_it_does: HTTP Toolkit intercepts HTTP(S) traffic with one-click capture for apps, devices, Docker containers, browsers, and backend processes such as Node.js, Java, Python, or Ruby, or it can be used as a manual HTTP proxy. It lets users search and filter captured messages and examine URLs, statuses, headers, and bodies, with autoformatting for formats like JSON, Protobuf, Base64, HTML, and XML. Breakpoints can pause live traffic to redirect, edit, respond to, or close requests. It also includes an HTTP client for sending custom requests and, as a Pro feature, automated rewrite rules for injecting mock responses, redirecting hosts, and injecting errors.
notable: One-click interception targeted at a single app, device, container, or browser window
Body viewing built on Monaco, the editor from Visual Studio Code
Breakpoints to pause and edit live traffic
Pro rewrite rules for mock responses and error injection
caveats: Automated rewrite rules (mock responses, transforms, error injection) are a Pro feature
Desktop platforms only: Windows, Linux, and Mac; mobile is used via a download link to the computer
